source_note: Dramatized from the public Valmiki Ramayana Aranya Kanda tradition. Verdicts label what we invent or compress. Do not invent theology as fact.

items.claim: Surpanakha desires Rama in the Dandaka forest and is refused; she is then mutilated (nose/ears) by Lakshmana.
items.source_note: Aranya Kanda; widely attested. Staging of the wound is ours (consequence, not spectacle).

items.claim: Khara and Dushana attack Rama after Surpanakha's report and are killed.
items.source_note: Aranya Kanda war episode; crowd scale is simplified.

items.claim: Surpanakha's speech in Lanka causes Ravana to desire Sita and plan the abduction.
items.source_note: Her report is traditional; the exact dialogue is dramatized.

items.claim: Maricha becomes the golden deer and, dying, cries out in Rama's voice.
items.source_note: Deer-Maya and the false cry are traditional.

items.claim: Lakshmana rekha — a magical line Lakshmana draws that Ravana cannot cross.
items.source_note: Popular later tradition / performance, not a secure Valmiki beat. We mark the threshold as a line Sita chooses to cross; do not present it as Valmiki fact.

items.claim: Ravana approaches as a mendicant/ascetic and seizes Sita.
items.source_note: Disguise as a holy beggar is traditional. Our rule: reader still sees Ravana.

items.claim: Jatayu fights Ravana in the sky, is mortally wounded, and later tells Rama who took Sita.
items.source_note: Aranya Kanda. Jewel-drop as a trail is traditional-adjacent; we use it as a continuity prop (simplified).

items.claim: Sita's jewelry falling from Pushpaka to mark the path.
items.source_note: Present in the tradition in various forms; we lock one necklace/earring set from the Sita bible.
We do not stage it. Capture is seizure and resistance, adult, not exploitation.
